frequency_question: How often do highly motivated states successfully domesticate complex missile production within 24 months?
membership_rule: Includes sovereign states attempting to stand up domestic manufacturing lines for guided missiles or cruise missiles during active conflict; excludes peacetime licensing agreements without urgent transfer pressure.

cases.name: UK production of Oerlikon and Bofors guns under emergency pressure (WWII)
Soviet relocation and establishment of tank/aircraft engine production lines behind the Urals
Iran domestic production of reverse-engineered guided anti-tank missiles under sanctions and war
South Korea emergency localized production of baseline artillery and rocket components
Ukraine domestic production ramp-up of Stugna-P anti-tank systems post-2014 invasion
Ukraine adaptation and scaled domestic production of long-range one-way attack drones (Neptune/FPV industrial scaling)
Taiwan Hsiung Feng cruise missile rapid domestic mass production initation

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 7 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 7 named cases spanning high-urgency sovereign ordnance localization; all 7 achieved operational domestic lines within the 2-year window due to extreme existential necessity overriding normal friction.
known_gaps: Historical reporting on classified missile localization efforts in smaller states may suffer from selection bias toward successes.
validity_reason: The fundamental dynamics of wartime state survival and urgent industrial mobilization remain stable across decades.
